_schema_doc: Single source of truth for what a release ships. `builds` names each
compiled artifact: its package, the exact cargo feature list it is
compiled with, and, for a CUDA build, the capability assertions a real
device must prove for it. `lanes` names each shipped artifact family,
the build it packages, the workflow job that promotes it, and the
workflows that build it (which the feature-literal guard reads).
A build is compiled once per tree, in `build.yml`, by the reusable workflow
that defines it; every lane packages those bytes, and a release promotes
the ones the run that proved its tree built. Two lanes of one build
therefore cannot ship different features; a lane whose features must
differ needs a build of its own.
The one compile site, `.github/workflows/_server.yml`, reads
`.builds.<build>.cargo_features` with `jq` rather than carrying a copy; a
container image packages the binary that site built and compiles
nothing. Each native wheel's `pyproject.toml` must list exactly its
build's features (`crates/jammi-db/tests/it/shipped_feature_exposure.rs`).
`ci/scripts/check_flash_attn_closure.py` asserts, for every build that
carries `capabilities`, that `capabilities.flash_compiled` matches
whether its `cargo_features` reach `jammi-kernels/flash-attn` in the
workspace feature graph. `ci/scripts/runpod_gpu_prove.sh` compiles with
the `server-cu12` list and derives the `jammi-ai`-applicable subset by
subtracting `server_only_cargo_features`.
`wheel_verifies_link_set` states, per server build, whether its wheel's
runtime link set is verified against the wheel's dependency wheels
(`packaging/<build>/verify_link_set.py`): true where the libraries arrive
as dependency wheels, false where the binary links only what manylinux
promises.
Adding a shipped artifact is a lane naming its build; adding a build is
an entry under `builds` and the lanes that package it.
`ci/scripts/check_release_manifest.py` fails on a lane that names no
build and on a build no lane packages.
`capabilities.fused_op_admission` vs `capabilities.internal_subkernels`:
these are TWO DIFFERENT PROOF MECHANISMS, not one list split by
convenience, and they are the ONLY two a capability block may carry.
Every op named across them appears in EXACTLY ONE — `ci/scripts/
check_release_manifest.py` enforces that, that neither category is
present but EMPTY, that no capability key outside the closed set below
appears at all, and that every build's `capabilities` block is identical
to every other build's. The non-category capability keys are exactly
`cuda_compiled`, `flash_compiled` and `flash_dtypes`: build facts about
the build, naming no op.
`fused_op_admission` is ONLY ops
`crates/jammi-ai/tests/gpu_capability/capability_surface.rs` can attribute
to a real `jammi_kernels::admission::{admit,admit_cascade}` dispatch-
registry key — that test reads THIS key (via `capabilities.
fused_op_admission`) and, for each op it maps, asserts a real
registry-counter DELTA around a live forward + backward + optimizer step
on a real CUDA device — a Fused dispatch that genuinely fired, not a
completed-run inference. Two entries (`softmax`, `rope`) are structurally
UNREACHABLE under `JAMMI_KERNELS_STRICT=1` through ModernBERT's attention
path once `attention_block_fused` admits — see that test's own
`STRICT_UNREACHABLE_OPS` doc — so the test logs them informationally
rather than asserting `Holds`; they stay listed here (removing them would
misrepresent them as never covered by fused-kernel authoring, which is
false — they DO have real registry keys, just not an independently
provable Strict-mode run through this attention path) but a manifest
consumer must not read every `fused_op_admission` entry as "asserted
Holds" without also reading that test's own per-op caveats.
An op is named here by its DTYPE-NEUTRAL name even when the registry keys
it actually dispatches under are dtype-keyed: `cast_scale` admits under
`cast_scale_bf16_f32`/`cast_scale_f16_f32` and `cast_add` under
`cast_add_bf16`/`cast_add_f16`, both through `admit_cast_boundary` in
`crates/jammi-kernels/src/ops/low_rank_residual_linear.rs` (called from
that op's BF16 and F16 backward arms). The report-name -> registry-key
mapping is a static table in `jammi-kernels` (`PROBED_OPS`), and
`capability_surface.rs` asserts set-equality between THIS file's
categories and that table by kind, so a name here that no table row maps
fails loudly instead of going silently unprobed. `adamw_step` is the
optimizer-step member of this category: it admits under
`adamw_step_fused` (`crates/jammi-ai/src/fine_tune/adamw.rs`'s `admit`
call), F32 ONLY — proven by the `capability_surface` probe's own real
optimizer step, which is exactly why that probe runs backward + one AdamW
step rather than a forward alone.
`internal_subkernels` is the DIFFERENT mechanism: an op with real CUDA
kernels and dispatch arms that is launched DIRECTLY by an admitted PARENT
op and has no `admit()`/`admit_cascade()` call of its own —
`rope_positions` (launched bare as `crate::cuda::rope_positions::cuda_fwd`
from the flash-attention op) and `scaled_cast_add` (constructed bare as
`ScaledCastAdd::new` in `low_rank_residual_linear`'s epilogue). Each entry
names its `parent` and its `launch_site` — by FILE, never a line number,
so the citation does not rot on an unrelated edit. Such an op is proven by
(1) compiling in this build and (2) its PARENT's admitted dispatch
being OBSERVED: a registry delta on the parent's key under
`JAMMI_KERNELS_STRICT=1` in the `capability_surface` probe. The parent
cannot have dispatched Fused without running the sub-kernel it launches
unconditionally. NEVER by a counter of its own — there is none. A
consumer must therefore read an entry here as neither "unreachable" NOR
"independently admitted": it is reached exactly when its parent is, and
carries no admission decision of its own to report. `parent` names the
identity whose observed delta IS the proof: `attention_block_flash` is the
flash cascade's registry key (this file's own `flash_compiled`/
`flash_dtypes` describe that build), and `low_rank_residual_linear` is a
`fused_op_admission` op above (registry key `lora_linear_fused`).
THERE IS NO COMPILED-ONLY CATEGORY. A kernel with no `admit()`/
`admit_cascade()` call site AND no admitted parent that launches it has NO
category here at all: the only thing a shipped build could say about it is
"it compiled", which is not a capability a consumer can act on, and a
category holding exactly that is an empty proof slot the next unwired
kernel gets filed into instead of being decided. Such a kernel is either
WIRED — given a real dispatch site, which lands it in
`fused_op_admission` — or DELETED, in the same unit as its authoring. The
decision is a measurement against a threshold fixed BEFORE the numbers are
seen, not a judgement call at review time; see `crates/jammi-kernels/
artifacts/cuda-runs/2026-09-01-axpy-census-bdeb80c-a100-pcie.json` for the
precedent, where a pre-registered rule (wire iff the op's share reaches 2%
of per-step GPU time on some shipped leg AND one dispatch site covers at
least half of that share) measured 0.007% / 0.026% / 0.027% across the
three shipped dtype legs and the kernel was deleted rather than kept as a
compiled-only row.
Promotion is always a code edit and a manifest edit in ONE unit: wiring a
real `admit()`/`admit_cascade()` call site (and its `PROBED_OPS` row)
promotes an op into `fused_op_admission`; giving it an admitted parent
that launches it directly moves it into `internal_subkernels`. Never a
manifest-only move.
A CPU build carries NO `capabilities` block: it reaches neither `cuda`
nor `flash-attn`, so it has no capability surface to declare.
`check_release_manifest.py` enforces `capabilities` present iff
`cargo_features` names `cuda` or `flash-attn`, forbidden otherwise
(syntactically); `check_flash_attn_closure.py` re-derives the same fact
from the real feature graph and skips a build with no `capabilities`
block by rule. `crates/jammi-db/tests/it/shipped_feature_exposure.rs`
covers the rest: every shipped family is a lane, each native wheel's
`pyproject.toml` builds exactly its build's features, the generated
`deny.toml` exposure line.

server-cpu._doc: The CPU `jammi-server` binary, built once per arch (x86_64, aarch64 Linux). The CPU tarball, PyPI wheel and container image each package it.

server-cu12._doc: The CUDA `jammi-server` binary (x86_64 Linux). The CUDA tarball, PyPI wheel and container image each package it.

native-cpu._doc: The embedded CPU engine (`jammi-python`), built by maturin from `packaging/native/pyproject.toml`, whose `[tool.maturin] features` beyond `extension-module` must equal this list (`crates/jammi-db/tests/it/shipped_feature_exposure.rs`). Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS.

native-cu12._doc: The embedded CUDA engine (`jammi-python`), built by maturin from `packaging/native-cu12/pyproject.toml`, whose `[tool.maturin] features` beyond `extension-module` must equal this list (`crates/jammi-db/tests/it/shipped_feature_exposure.rs`). Linux x86_64. The same kernels as `server-cu12`, so the same capability surface.

cu12-tarball._doc: The self-contained CUDA `jammi-server` tarball: the binary, the CUDA runtime `.so`s it links, and an `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` launcher.

cpu-tarball._doc: The CPU `jammi-server` tarball, x86_64 and aarch64 Linux.

cpu-wheel._doc: The `jammi-server` PyPI wheel (CPU), x86_64 and aarch64.

cpu-image._doc: The `jammi-ai-server` container image, its `generic` and `selfcontained` variants (the Dockerfile's `runtime-generic`/`runtime-selfcontained` stages).
cpu-image.workflow: .github/workflows/server-image.yml:push-cpu, packaging the binary .github/workflows/_server.yml builds; the image smokes .github/workflows/kube-smoke.yml and .github/workflows/compose-smoke.yml package the same binary

native-cpu-wheel._doc: The `jammi-ai-native` PyPI wheel (the embedded CPU engine).

native-cu12-wheel._doc: The `jammi-ai-native-cu12` PyPI wheel (the embedded CUDA engine).

_doc: Features that exist on `jammi-server` with no `jammi-ai` equivalent
(cloud-storage plumbing and the external-database source drivers the
embedded engine crate does not carry). A consumer deriving the
`jammi-ai`-applicable subset of a build's `cargo_features` (e.g.
`runpod_gpu_prove.sh`'s capability-surface build, which runs `cargo test
-p jammi-ai --features <subset>` rather than `-p jammi-server`)
subtracts this list from `builds.<build>.cargo_features`. Every CUDA
build resolves to `["cuda", "flash-attn"]` on `jammi-ai` once these are
removed, every CPU build to `[]`.
Proof surface == shipped surface: the DECLARED set of `(crate, kind)`
pairs `ci/scripts/runpod_gpu_prove.sh` must invoke on a real device.
`kind` is one of `release` (a `cargo build --release`/`cargo run
--release` invocation), `test` (a `cargo test` invocation carrying a
`--features` tuple, with or without `--no-run`), or `default` (a `cargo
test` invocation with NO `--features` flag at all -- canonicalizes to an
empty feature list). `ci/scripts/prove_surface.py` computes, for a
declared pair, `expected(crate, kind) = (this file's own
`builds.server-cu12.cargo_features` ∩ crate's OWN `[features]` table
keys) ∪ (this entry's `prove_only`, iff kind == test)` -- read
hermetically via stdlib `tomllib`, never a second hardcoded copy of a
crate's feature list. `check_flash_attn_closure.py` asserts SET EQUALITY
between THIS declared pair set and the script's own invocations (one
literal tuple text per pair, preceded by a `PROVE_TUPLE` echo) -- a
dropped `--features`, a deleted proof invocation, or an unlisted pair
each FAIL. `prove_only` names a feature the shipped lane does not itself
require but the PROOF needs to actually exercise the gated suite
(`live-gpu-tests` gates every real-device `#[test]` in this workspace)
-- it is added only to a `test`-kind pair, never to `release` (a release
build ships exactly the lane's own features, nothing test-only).
